fields.v: Huang, V. S.-J., Li, R., Yin, Z., Mao, K., Zhao, Y., Wang, X., Yin, Y., Luo, L., Zhang, R., Li, H. (2026). SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces. arXiv:2610.32196v1 [cs.AI], 23 Oct 2026
Preprint — arXiv:2610.32196v1 (23 Oct 2026); no published venue stated (record only in the arXiv export)

MMLab, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Huang, Zhang, Li); Fudan NLP Lab, Fudan University (Yin Z., Wang); The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Zhao); Peking University (Yin Y., Luo); affiliation 5 printed as 'Somewhere on the Earth' (Li R., Mao)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — introduces the SWE-Shift benchmark (120 scenarios with task-relevant mid-execution changes, matched Clean and Shifted continuations from the same saved state) and evaluates 17 coding-agent systems on it

No SDD approach. Coding-agent systems compared (model + harness): Codex app with GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.6 Sol; Claude Code app with Claude Opus 5 and Claude Fable 5.1 (all xhigh reasoning; app versions Not stated); 13 open-weight models (Kimi-K3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, DeepSeek V4-Flash, Kimi-K2.6, MiniMax-M3, GLM-5.3-Flash, MiniMax-M2.7, Devstral-2-123B-Instruct, Agents-A1, Qwen3.8-27B, MiMo-V2.5-Pro, Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen3-Coder-Next) served locally with vLLM 0.27.1/0.28.0/0.28.1rc1 or SGLang 0.5.17 and driven by the benchmark runner (structured file actions, named commands, declared state operations; runner not named)
N/A (no SDD approach). Each scenario specifies the repository task, an authorized mid-execution update, how the agent can discover it, and held-out executable checks

N/A (no SDD flow). Benchmark protocol: agent runs a shared prefix -> checkpoint saved at one of nine positions T10-T90 -> state restored twice -> Clean continuation (no update) and Shifted continuation (update applied) -> held-out checks on final workspace and event history
None (autonomous agents; updates delivered by the runner)
N/A (no SDD approach; full agent runs)
Not classifiable (benchmark of coding agents, no specification approach); authors do not use SDD terms. Families F08 (disclosure), F10 (goal revision) change requirements mid-run

Existing code bases: repository issue tasks from SWE-bench Verified (60 scenarios), Multi-SWE-bench (35) and SWE-bench Multilingual (25), with a task-relevant change introduced during execution (12 change families)

120 scenarios (10 per change family, 12 families), 23 task-root snapshots from 17 repositories, 39 family-archetype-root clusters; 9 intervention positions = 1,080 cells per system; repository size Not stated
Open-source repositories (e.g. astropy, django, scikit-learn, sympy, sphinx, pylint, apache/druid, tokio-rs/bytes, caddy, grpc-go, express, fluentd); domain Not stated
N/A (no human participants; autonomous agents)
None measured as an outcome. Post-fork token budget fixed at B = 1,000,000 input+output tokens per continuation (varied B/2-16B only in a diagnostic control); no time or money

Clean success, Shifted success, Paired Success Rate (PSR: both continuations succeed, or verified completion before the intervention) and Conditional Retention Rate (CRR: joint success / Clean success); a continuation succeeds only if every applicable check passes (task, preservation, recovery, authority, prohibited effects, fresh observation, budget, terminal integrity)
None
None

PSR by change family and by intervention position; diagnostic controls (change notice, read-only state refresh, removal of pre-change history; post-fork token budget sensitivity) on five systems; qualitative audit of 24 GPT-5.6 Sol trajectories

Automatic: held-out executable checks on workspace, controller and modeled adapters plus the event history (action order, external effects); hierarchical family-cluster-scenario weighting; scenarios pre-validated with admission checks (Table 3; all 120 T0 cases and 1,080 cells pass). Manual: qualitative audit of 24 cases. Benchmark construction assisted by OpenAI Codex; initial 24 cases built and audited with GPT-5.6 Sol

Verdicts: quality: no criterion stated by the authors (all configurations); cost: not measured

Tasks: 120 scenarios x 9 intervention positions. Configurations: 17 model-agent systems. Baseline: matched Clean continuation from the same saved prefix (per system). Held constant: scenarios, positions, available tools, post-fork token budget (1M); open-weight systems T=0, p=1, 131,072 context, 4,096 max output; provider systems in their native apps at xhigh (harness not held constant across systems). Acceptance tests: held-out executable checks, scenarios validated before evaluation. Repetitions: Not stated (point values; 'model randomness remains uncontrolled'). Human intervention: none; infrastructure-faulted cells retried with labels kept

All 17 systems have lower Shifted than Clean success; GPT-6 Astra best (Clean 67.35 -> Shifted 24.79, PSR 20.34, CRR 30.20). Tool/session changes (F06) and stale evidence (F11): PSR 0.00% for all 17; runtime/resources (F05) zero for 16 of 17; disclosure (F08) zero for 13 of 17 (Claude Fable 5.1 16.20%, GPT-6 Astra 14.90%). Higher Clean does not imply higher retention (Kimi-K2.6 highest CRR 34.63% with Clean 20.50%). Timing: T70-T90 vs T10-T30 PSR -20.05 pts GPT-6 Astra, -15.43 Fable 5.1, -12.53 GPT-5.6 Sol, -11.93 Opus 5; +2.97 GLM-5.3-Flash, +2.20 Kimi-K2.6, +1.60 DeepSeek V4-Flash. No significance tests

Distinguished systems, change families and timing profiles; matched continuations separate failure on the underlying task from loss of success after the change. Repeatability: not assessed (single point values, randomness uncontrolled). Limitations stated: 120 designed scenarios, some sharing task roots; one update per run; diagnostic controls on five systems only; intervention position reflects execution stage, not semantic progress; fixed post-fork token budget

Limitations: designed scenarios sharing roots, one update per run, diagnostics on five systems, uncontrolled model randomness, positions not normalized progress, fixed token budget. Gaps: evaluating repeated changes in natural software-development workflows; checking preservation and evidence validity alongside task completion

Code and data: https://github.com/JeixHuang/SWE-Shift (data/results.json, controls.json, benchmark.json, model-cards.json). Benchmark data selection and construction assisted by OpenAI Codex, and the initial 24 cases were constructed and audited with GPT-5.6 Sol (an evaluated system); possible bias not discussed. Affiliation 5 printed as 'Somewhere on the Earth'. Codex app and Claude Code app versions not stated; open-weight harness not named. rev.why: Most authors are at universities, but two authors (Li R., Mao) give the affiliation 'Somewhere on the Earth', so their independence from the evaluated vendors cannot be checked; the paper also used OpenAI Codex and GPT-5.6 Sol (an evaluated system) to build and audit the benchmark. Yes kept as best value since nothing links any author to a vendor.

No author is linked to OpenAI, Anthropic or the open-weight model vendors, but two authors (Li R., Mao) give 'Somewhere on the Earth' as affiliation (p. 1), so their independence cannot be checked; under the missing-information rule another reader could score Partly. Yes kept as best value.
